subject: Acme Health pilot - short quarantine & autoscale exception request
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Acme Health pilot - short quarantine & autoscale exception request

Team —

Acme is planning a 72-hour load validation window for the Dedicated pilot next week (May 12–14). They want a short "quarantine" of a small GPU pool so their traffic doesn't contend with other pilots while we validate multipart requests + long-context behaviour.

Asks:
- Temporary autoscale exception to prevent preemption/eviction during the window (3 days).
- Reserve a 4-GPU slice (preferably 2xA40 or equivalent) with a hard cap; we can drop to 2 GPUs after validation.
- A short mutual action plan: who watches the logs, rollback criteria, and an ops contact for on-call.

Attachments: acme-loadplan-202605.pdf (traffic profile + schedule) and capacity-estimates.xlsx.

Why: their test profile includes repeated long-context generations and KV cache warmups that would get noisy if slices were preempted mid-run. This is a short, high-value proof-of-concept tied to DL-4931.

Can infra confirm constraints and ops handoff? Product — any objections from product policy or SLO side?

Thanks,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Account Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-04T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme Health pilot - short quarantine & autoscale exception request

Naomi —

Thanks for the heads up. A couple quick clarifying questions from Product:
- Is Acme expecting any SLA delta (latency/availability) versus our standard Dedicated offering during this window?
- What's their acceptance criteria for the validation (error rate threshold, latency targets, success calls per second)?
- Do we need to pin a model binary/version or will they test against our rolling model catalog?

If there are SLA changes we should capture them in a short SOW addendum. Happy to sync and draft the MAP once Marcus confirms feasibility.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Product, Dedicated

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-04T11:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme Health pilot - short quarantine & autoscale exception request

Naomi / team —

We can support a short, isolated carve for the dates requested. Some notes and constraints:

1) Capacity options:
   - Preferred: 2 x A40-equivalent GPUs (nice balance for long-context perf); reserves 4 vGPU slots (in our accounting this will appear as a 4-GPU slice).
   - Alternate: 4 x T4 (lower cost, lower p99 tail performance for long-context).

2) Autoscale exception: we can disable preemption for that slice for up to 96 hours. We will need an explicit maintenance window and a kill-switch (ops-controlled) if cluster pressure gets to >85% util across the availability zone.

3) Operational runbook:
   - On-call: infra on-call (primary: Marcus) + ops engineer (TBD by Naomi).
   - Rollback: if p95 latency exceeds 1.5x baseline or error rate >2% sustained for 10m, we abort and re-snapshot.

4) Accounting: this will be charged as reserved capacity for the 3-day window (we'll pro-rate off the monthly dedicated pool). Dev — can you confirm pricing/discount path?

I attached a quick capacity-estimates.xlsx sheet with projected token/slot utilization under the two hardware options.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Infrastructure

From: Alex Jensen <alex.jensen@acme.health>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Ortiz <sam.ortiz@acme.health>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-05T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme Health pilot - short quarantine & autoscale exception request

Hi Naomi / Kimberly —

Thanks — we confirm the planned window May 12–14 and prefer the A40 option if available. Acceptance criteria (short):
- Sustained 30 RPS for the model pipeline for 10m windows during peak load tests.
- p95 latency under 450ms for single-turn prompts (we understand long-context will be higher).
- Zero preemption during any test run.

We can share a short SOW addendum with acceptance criteria and will sign for a temporary reserved slice for the 3 days. Sam will be the ops contact for the run.

Attached is our updated load plan with expected burst patterns. Let us know the next steps for MAP and any procurement paperwork.

—Alex
Alex Jensen
Product Lead, Acme Health

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Jensen <alex.jensen@acme.health>
Date: 2026-05-05T13:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme Health pilot - short quarantine & autoscale exception request

Folks —

Pricing side: we can offer a short-term reserved carve at a 20% pro-rated premium to standard Dedicated hourly rates (covers the no-preempt guarantee + ops time). If Acme signs the SOW addendum by May 9 we can lock capacity.

Procurement timeline: we need PO + signed addendum. I'll attach the SOW draft (acme-sow-draft-v2.docx) for Naomi to share. No legal redlines expected for a 3-day window; finance will do a quick check.

Next actions I propose:
- Naomi: confirm Acme signs addendum by May 9.
- Marcus: provision the slice in staging and run a smoke test by May 10.
- Kimberly: draft the MAP and acceptance criteria in a 1-pager.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jensen <alex.jensen@acme.health>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, finance@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-06T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme Health pilot - short quarantine & autoscale exception request

Alex / team —

Summary and next steps (confirming):
- Acme will sign SOW addendum by May 9 (Alex to confirm with procurement).
- Redwood will reserve 2xA40-equivalent slice for May 12–14 and disable preemption for that slice. Marcus to provision and run smoke test by May 10.
- MAP owner: Kimberly to produce a 1-page runbook (due May 10). Ops contact: Sam Ortiz (Acme) + Marcus infra on-call.
- Pricing: Dev to issue the pro-rated invoice at 20% premium for the three-day reservation.

Attachments sent in thread: acme-loadplan-202605.pdf, acme-sow-draft-v2.docx, capacity-estimates.xlsx.

If anyone sees an issue, flag here. Otherwise I’ll share the SOW and MAP links with Acme and close the loop.

Thanks — looking forward to a successful test window.

Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Account Lead, Redwood Inference
